question: A persistent, non-healing warty or ulcerating lesion on the glans or prepuce that has not improved after two courses of antibiotics should be biopsied promptly to exclude penile carcinoma.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. A non-healing ulcer or warty lesion on the penis that fails to respond to antibiotics must be biopsied; carcinoma of the penis can masquerade as infection for months, and delay worsens prognosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A non-healing penile lesion is carcinoma until proven otherwise; empirical antibiotic courses that fail are a red flag. Biopsy is mandatory — penile squamous cell carcinoma is associated with HPV, chronic inflammation (lichen sclerosus, phimosis), and poor circumcision status.
